article_title: Usage of augmented reality (AR) and development of e-learning outcomes: An empirical evaluation of students’ e-learning experience
citation: Baabdullah, Alsulaimani, Allamnakhrah, Alalwan, Dwivedi & Rana. (2021). Usage of Augmented Reality (AR) and Development of e-Learning Outcomes: An Empirical Evaluation of Students' e-Learning Experience. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Usage+of+Augmented+Reality+AR+and+Development+of+e-Learning+Outcomes+An+Empirical+Evaluation+of+Students+e-Learning+Experience
title: UGT-based conceptual model of students' e-learning experience with augmented reality learning applications
description: The article adapts Uses and Gratifications Theory (Katz et al., 1974) into a conceptual model in which four UGT benefit dimensions — "personal integrative benefits (PIB); cognitive benefits (CGB); social integrative benefits (SIB); and affective benefits (AB)" — act as antecedents of students' e-learning experience with AR learning applications, which in turn drives e-learning performance. The model extends UGT with telepresence as an additional antecedent and technostress as a moderator of all four benefit-experience paths. It was operationalised as a two-stage SEM model with 34 scale items across eight latent constructs and tested on 325 valid survey responses.
requirements: Respondents must be actively engaged in using AR learning applications for the experience constructs to be meaningful
constraints: Tested with undergraduate students at four large Saudi universities in science, computer science, engineering and medicine disciplines; the article does not claim generalisation beyond this context
target_learning_goals: positive e-learning experience with augmented reality learning applications
examples: The model was validated via a questionnaire survey of 500 approached undergraduates (325 valid, 65% response rate) using seven-point Likert scales, with measurement and structural model fit indices reported
